Lesson · 25 min

Tables, Images, Smart Chips, and Voice Typing

Add tables and images, insert smart chips for people, dates, and files, drop in building blocks like meeting notes, and dictate with voice typing.

By the end of this lesson you can

  • ✓Insert a table, type in it, and add or delete rows and columns
  • ✓Insert an image from your computer, Drive and Photos, or a URL
  • ✓Insert smart chips for a person, a date, and a file with @ or Insert › Smart chips
  • ✓Add a building block such as Meeting notes
  • ✓Start voice typing with Tools › Voice typing

Lesson Notes

Read through the key concepts before you try the challenge.

Tables

On the job

You write the weekly maintenance update for Elm Street Apartments.

Kim Nguyen sends you the week's repairs in a text message, and Denise wants them in a tidy update: who prepared it, the date, a table of repairs, a photo of the finished work, and a link to the vendor list.

Your task: Build the update with a table, an image, and smart chips.

  • Click where the table goes, then Insert › Table and point to the size you want (columns x rows). Tables can be up to 20 x 20.
  • Click a cell to type. Press Tab to move to the next cell.
  • Right-click a cell for Insert row above, Insert row below, Insert column left, Insert column right, Delete row, Delete column, and Delete table.
  • Format › Table › Table options sets sizes, cell padding, and alignment. Under Row, Pin header row(s) repeats the header row on each page.
  • Right-click the table › Sort table to sort the rows in ascending or descending order.

Images

  • Click where the image goes, then Insert › Image and choose a source: Upload from computer, Stock & web, Drive & Photos, Camera, or By URL.
  • You can also drag an image file from your computer into the document.
  • Click the image to see its options: In line, Wrap text, Break text, Behind text, or In front of text. Drag a corner to resize it.
  • Only use images you have the right to use. Photos Parkview took, and the stock images Docs offers, are safe choices.
In a pageless document, the text-wrapping layouts are not available; images stay in line with the text.

Smart chips and building blocks

A smart chip is a small, clickable box in the text for a person, a date, a file, a place, or a calendar event. Type @ anywhere in a document (or use Insert › Smart chips) and pick from the list. Hovering over a people chip shows the person's details; clicking a file chip opens the file.

A people chip does not share the document with that person. If they need to open it, share it with them separately.

Building blocks are ready-made pieces: Insert › Building blocks, or type @ and choose one. Meeting notes adds notes filled in with the details of a Google Calendar event you pick. Email draft adds an email with a To field, a subject, and a body that you can write together; when it is ready, click Preview in Gmail at the top left of the draft to open it in Gmail and send it.

Voice typing

  1. Click where the text should go, then Tools › Voice typing. A microphone box appears.
  2. Click the microphone (allow the browser to use it the first time) and speak clearly.
  3. Say punctuation out loud: period, comma, exclamation point, question mark, new line, new paragraph.
  4. Click the microphone again to stop. Check what was typed and fix mistakes.
Voice typing works in the latest versions of Chrome, Edge, and Safari. Voice commands such as punctuation work only when the account and document language are English.

Challenge

Apply what you've learned in this lesson.

Build a one-page update in your own Google account.

  1. Create a document named Weekly Update - your name. Type Prepared by: and insert a people chip for yourself (type @ and your name).
  2. Type Date: and insert @today.
  3. Insert a 3 x 3 table and fill in a header row (Task, Status, Notes) and two rows.
  4. Insert an image from Stock & web.
  5. Insert the Meeting notes building block at the end. Then try Tools › Voice typing to dictate one sentence (skip this step if your computer has no microphone).
Deliverable: Submit a PDF of your update to your instructor or course folder. No Google account? Complete the practice simulation and submit its results page.
